summary: Practise protection risk analysis, referrals, and response planning for emergencies. Explore the five-day course and strengthen your operational approach.
lede: Human rights and protection in disasters help humanitarian responders assess risks and plan safer services. Designed for protection officers, emergency programme leads, and response coordinators, the course covers prioritizing protection risks, mapping safe referrals, and planning community feedback. It also addresses displacement, child protection, disability inclusion, and careful handling of sensitive response information.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for humanitarian and emergency response professionals who make or support decisions affecting safety, dignity, access to assistance, and protection referrals.
modules: IASC Protection Policy in Disaster Response
Sphere Standards for Protection Risk Analysis
Core Humanitarian Standard and Community Feedback
IASC Gender Handbook and Safe Referral
IASC Disability Inclusion in Relief Operations
prerequisites: Recommended preparation: experience in humanitarian, disaster response, protection, or emergency programme work, plus basic familiarity with human rights concepts. No coding or programming is required.
